faqs.question: What is the difference between anticipatory bail and regular bail in Delhi?
faqs.answer: Anticipatory bail is sought before arrest when a person apprehends arrest in a non-bailable offence, granting protection from custody. Regular bail is applied for after a person has already been arrested or surrendered before the court.

faqs.question: Can an FIR be quashed by the Delhi High Court?
faqs.answer: Yes. Under Section 482 CrPC (now Section 528 BNSS), the High Court of Delhi has inherent powers to quash an FIR where the allegations do not disclose any offence, where the complaint is purely frivolous or malicious, or where parties in matrimonial or private disputes have reached an amicable settlement.

faqs.question: What is the timeline for filing a Section 138 cheque bounce case in Delhi?
faqs.answer: The cheque must be presented within 3 months of issuance. Upon dishonour, a legal demand notice must be dispatched within 30 days of receiving the bank memo. The drawer has 15 days from receipt to pay. If they fail to pay, the complaint must be filed in court within 30 days thereafter.

faqs.question: Can I claim interim compensation in a cheque bounce case in Delhi courts?
faqs.answer: Yes. Under Section 143A of the NI Act, the Magistrate Court can direct the drawer to pay interim compensation of up to 20% of the cheque amount to the complainant during the trial itself.

faqs.question: What is the procedure to appeal an adverse income tax assessment order?
faqs.answer: An appeal against an assessment order must be filed before the Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals) [CIT(A)] within 30 days of service of the demand notice. If dissatisfied with the CIT(A) order, a second appeal lies before the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT Delhi) within 60 days.

faqs.question: Can I challenge a SARFAESI possession notice in DRT Delhi?
faqs.answer: Yes. Once the bank issues a notice under Section 13(4) or obtains a Chief Metropolitan Magistrate (CMM) order under Section 14 to take physical possession, the borrower or guarantor can file a Securitisation Application (SA) under Section 17 before the DRT within 45 days to seek a stay.
